prerequisites: Theoretical knowledge in the field of differential and integral calculus with one variable.
Ability to solve applied problems in differential and integral calculus with one variable.
Ability to solve linear algebra problems.
Ability to independently organize the necessary learning environment and to independently solve tasks with the available tools.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are provided with fundamental knowledge of mathematics so that they can adequately address problems in subsequent modules.
Knowledge of the theory of the mathematical topics listed below, as far as it is relevant for application-oriented use in engineering.
Knowledge of mathematical methods for the topics listed below for solving problems specifically for engineering questions.
Practical experience gained through practice in the application-oriented use of what has been learned to problems.
Ability to independently develop advanced mathematical tools for engineering.
Both independent acquisition of knowledge and self-organization for solving tasks.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to specify complex functions and fundamental integral transformations.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to describe essential properties of Fourier series, Sturm-Liouville boundary value problems, and partial differential equations.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to apply methods of complex function theory and integral transformations to engineering problems.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to process Fourier series and suitable procedures for solving Sturm-Liouville boundary value problems.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to present basic principles of randomness as well as methods for estimating parameters, confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to transfer methods of variance analysis and regression analysis to given datasets.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to analyze complex mathematical problems.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to select relevant statistical and function-theoretic tools for further engineering applications.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to analyze advanced mathematical tools of engineering sciences using case studies in individual, partner, and group work.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to justify their own calculation method in calculation examples.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to calculate solutions taking into account quality requirements.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to independently analyze improvements.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to implement improvements based on peer feedback.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to compare their own calculation methods with others.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to select learning and examination strategies.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to analyze results.

syllabus_topics: Complex function theory and integral transformations
Fourier series and Sturm-Liouville boundary value problems
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical foundations and basic instruments

assessment_methods.method: Written examination with calculation examples and theory questions
